newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico journalists to march to protest killing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico journalists to march to protest killing.

text.p: Mexican journalists in the troubled state of Guerrero plan to march again on Monday to protest the killing of one of their colleagues, a spokesman for the union of reporters said on Saturday.
Jesus Bueno Leon, director at the regional weekly Siete Dias, was found shot dead on a rural road close to the city of Chilpancingo some 120 miles (200 km) south of Mexico City on Thursday.
About 50 journalists marched in the streets of the port of Acapulco on Friday to protest the killing and to demand the killer or killers be found.
Members of the National Union of Press Reporters plan to take to the streets again, this time in the city of Chilpancingo on Monday, said union spokesman Ciricao Zacarlas Cervantes.
Members of the peasant organisation, the Farmer Organisation of the Sierra of the South, on Saturday also expressed their consternation to the killing.
Bueno said in a letter written before he died that his work had angered officials in his troubled home state of Guerrero.
He listed seven possible leads for police to investigate in case he was killed.
In a news release governor Aguirre Rivero expressed his profound consternation and condemned the slaying.
Chilpancingo is the state capital of Guerrero, a southern state with guerrilla activity, widespread kidnappings and frequent political and social unrest.
